name: map
description: Spec-to-task correlation layer. Owns the task journal, the append-only event log that links spec node identity hashes to tracker task ids — reads, folds, and the single append primitive every journal writer uses. Provides context resolution and the CLI query interface.

requirements.name: Store mapping records
requirements.description: Own the task journal — one JSON object per line, append-only, living inside the .spex/ state directory at the location the lifecycle resolver answers. Change events record what a baselining absorbed — node identity hash, name, node_type, module, before/after leaf hashes, git_head, proposal — the registered event records the opening of a proposal's lifecycle, and receipt events record what the tracker did (task_created/task_closed with a task id, refresh receipts naming absorbed events). MappingStore is the journal's one writer-owner: every append — ingest's reconciliation and refresh batches, the Registrar's registered event — goes through its atomic, schema-validating append primitive; nothing writes around it. Current linkage is a fold, never a stored cache: the latest task-bearing event per node, with the epic's entry sourced from its registered event. No metadata is denormalized; names and modules are read from the event that carried them.

requirements.name: Query mappings via CLI
requirements.description: spex map get returns structured JSON for one node — keyed by identity hash or task id; there is no integer record id. spex map list shows the folded current linkage. spex map context resolves full spec context for a node, live or removed. All four invocations are declared as api nodes — the parent `spex map` and its three children — and each names MapCommand in provided_by alongside the worker it drives: MappingStore for get and list, ContextResolver for context. A declared name carries no argument placeholder: the api is `spex map get`, not `spex map get <key>`, because the name must be the string a caller types and must survive corpus tokenization unchanged. Declaring the children alongside the parent is also what keeps the parent retirable — the removal-time name check discards hits that a longer live name already covers, so the mentions of `spex map` that belong to `spex map get`, `spex map list` or `spex map context` are never counted against the bare parent.

requirements.name: Validate mapping file against schema
requirements.description: MappingStore validates each journal line against the journal-line JSON Schema on read. A malformed line is a clear error from the map query surface, naming the line number. Gating commands are exempt by design: they treat an unreadable journal as absent and degrade detection, never fail — the journal is not load-bearing for the pipeline.

requirements.name: Resolve full spec context from record
requirements.description: Given an identity hash or a task id, deterministically resolve all spec files needed to implement the node, plus the event bracket that locates its latest change in git — eid, event, before_head, after_head — for any node, live or removed. A live node's files resolve from the spec alone: the arch file from the component's declared content, test_sections whose describes array contains the component ID, data_flows whose uses array contains it, and the module file — all derived, nothing read from a cache; its bracket comes from the journal: the latest task-bearing event's git_head against the git_head of the node's preceding change event, before_head null when the latest event is an added, the whole bracket null when the node has no task-bearing event yet. A removed node resolves from the journal: its name, node_type, module, the proposal that removed it, and the same bracket off its removed event. Returns a single JSON blob.

requirements.name: Fold and bracket retargeted tasks
requirements.description: task_retargeted is task-bearing: MappingStore's fold treats it exactly as it treats task_created — latest-wins moves the pairing's sourcing event forward to the retargeted event's referent, so the current linkage always points at the newest state the task owes. ContextResolver widens the context bracket for a retargeted task: before_head comes from the sourcing event of the task's original task_created, after_head from its latest task_retargeted event, so the implementer sees the full accumulated diff rather than the last increment. No path recreates a task with a lineage edge — an open task is retargeted, and a completed one is followed by a plain create whose only tie to its predecessor is the journal — so no blocks edge exists between generations anywhere in the tracker: the accumulation lives in the journal and this fold-and-bracket rule is what surfaces it.

components.name: MappingStore
components.description: Owner of the task journal: parse, scan, fold and append it at its resolved location. Change events and receipt events link spec node identity hashes to task ids; the fold — latest task-bearing event per node, task_created and task_retargeted alike — is the current linkage every consumer derives, never a stored cache. The node key is the same 12-char hex identity hash the merkle tree uses, so every pipeline stage looks events up by that hash with no translation. The store owns the journal's one append primitive — atomic write-and-rename, each line schema-validated before the write commits; ingest's reconciliation and refresh batches and the proposal Registrar's registered event all write through it, and nothing writes around it.

components.name: MapCommand
components.description: CLI entry point for spex map. Wires MappingStore and ContextResolver to serve queries and context resolution. The context payload carries the node's event bracket — eid, event, before_head, after_head — alongside the file set, keyed by identity hash or task id as before; existing keys keep their meaning, so the output is a superset of the pre-bracket shape.

components.name: ContextResolver
components.description: Given an identity hash or a task id, resolves all spec files for the node plus its event bracket — eid, event, before_head, after_head — for any node, live or removed. A live node's files resolve from the spec alone by matching the hash against ids declared in module.json — the arch file, the test_sections and data_flows that name it, and the module file itself; nothing is read from a cache. Its bracket comes from the journal: the latest task-bearing event's git_head against the preceding change event's, before_head null for an added, the whole bracket null when no task-bearing event exists. A retargeted task's bracket widens: before_head from the sourcing event of its original task_created, after_head from its latest task_retargeted event, so the whole accumulated change is in view. A removed node resolves from the journal: name, node_type, module, removing proposal, and the same bracket off its removed event. Pure function over spec directory plus journal — deterministic and cacheable.

data_flows.name: Task creation mapping flow
data_flows.description: How a task pairs with the event that spawned it. Plan derives each create op's journal eid at changeset-build time — the same (git_head, op_id) derivation ingest uses to mint the event — and stamps it on the op as the spex:<eid> idempotency label, an adapter that implements the optional label surface applies that label to the task it creates — or, for a retarget op, adds the new modified event's label to the existing task — and ingest appends the change event and its task_created (or task_retargeted) receipt through MappingStore at baselining. The journal records what the pipeline did, never a task's completion: a completed task's successor is a plain create paired by a fresh event, with no task_closed for the predecessor. Skills query the resulting linkage via MapCommand.

apis.name: spex map get
apis.description: Get one node's journal linkage by identity hash or task id

apis.name: spex map context
apis.description: Resolve full spec context for a spec node, live or removed
